```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helpers.R")
```

Settings Sync only carries what is inside VS Code ([what it does not carry](profiles_sync.qmd#what-settings-sync-does-not-carry)). The rest lives in a few small files. I keep them in the OneDrive `Documents` folder, so OneDrive shares them between my machines. Because they are shared, they follow the same rule as the VS Code settings: **no user names, and nothing that exists on only one machine unless it is checked first.**

## `.Rprofile` {#rprofile}

R runs a user `.Rprofile` at start-up. Which file R reads is subtle:

1. A `.Rprofile` in the **current folder**, if there is one. Otherwise:
2. the one in `R_USER`, which on Windows is the `Documents` folder (with OneDrive folder backup, that is `OneDrive\Documents`).
3. In **renv projects**, the project's own `.Rprofile` activates renv, and renv does **not** load the user `.Rprofile` unless you set `renv.config.user.profile = TRUE`. So none of the below applies inside renv projects (which includes projects from my [project template](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/Project_template)).

Point 1 bit me: old copies of `.Rprofile` in my home folder and in `C:\Users\<me>\Documents` silently replaced the real one whenever R started in those folders (and the home folder is a VS Code workspace). Keep **one** user `.Rprofile`. Check which one wins with `Sys.getenv("R_USER")` and `file.exists(".Rprofile")`.

### What it does, block by block

| Block | What it does | Why |
|---|---|---|
| httpgd in VS Code | Only when interactive and inside VS Code (`TERM_PROGRAM == "vscode"`) and if httpgd is installed: sets `vsc.rstudioapi`, `vsc.use_httpgd`, `vsc.plot = FALSE`, and makes httpgd the default graphics device. | Every plot goes to the httpgd viewer in VS Code. `vsc.rstudioapi` lets packages that call `rstudioapi` (add-ins, `usethis`) work in VS Code. |
| btw | Starts `btw::btw_mcp_session()` when interactive **and** btw is installed for this R version. | Lets coding assistants (through MCP) see the live R session: objects, help, installed packages. The check matters because each R version has its own library: on a fresh R version without btw, an unconditional call fails at every start-up. |
| radian options | `radian.auto_match = FALSE`, `radian.auto_indentation = FALSE`. | radian would otherwise insert closing brackets and indent as you type. Code sent from the editor is already complete and formatted, so the console should take it as it is. |
| RStudio's pandoc | Sets `RSTUDIO_PANDOC` to RStudio's bundled pandoc folder, if it exists. | rmarkdown outside RStudio then finds pandoc without a separate install. |
| Temporary folder | Sets `TEMP`/`TMP` to `D:/Temp`, **only if** that folder exists. | Big temporary files go to a second drive on the machine that has one. On other machines nothing changes. |
| TinyTeX | Appends TinyTeX's `bin\windows` to `PATH`, if installed and not there yet. | PDF output from R Markdown / Quarto started from R. |

Quarto is deliberately **not** set here (no `QUARTO_PATH`). The quarto R package and rmarkdown find Quarto on `PATH`, which is the [all-users install](install.qmd#quarto). An earlier version of this file forced an old per-user Quarto through `QUARTO_PATH` and quietly kept using it after an upgrade.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file("Rprofile.R", "r", label = ".Rprofile")
```

(Published as `Rprofile.R` so that browsers show it; save it as `.Rprofile` in your `Documents` folder.)

## radian

radian has its own profile file (`~/.radian_profile`), but I do not use one: the two options I change are R options, so they are in `.Rprofile` above. radian finds R in this order:

1. `--r-binary`, `R_BINARY` or `R_HOME`, if set;
2. `R` on `PATH`, which is rig's default version;
3. the Windows registry (`HKLM\Software\R-Core\R\InstallPath`).

So `R_HOME` must **not** be set globally ([PATH rules](#path-rules)).

## PowerShell {#powershell}

PowerShell 7 reads two profile files from `Documents\PowerShell\`. Both are shared through OneDrive.

`profile.ps1` (all PowerShell hosts) was written by `rig system fix-r-alias`. It removes the built-in `r` alias (`Invoke-History`), so that typing `R` starts R:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file("powershell/profile.ps1", "powershell")
```

`Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` (the console and VS Code terminals) loads [Oh My Posh](https://ohmyposh.dev/), a prompt theme that shows the git branch and status. It needs `winget install JanDeDobbeleer.OhMyPosh` and, for the icons, a [Nerd Font](https://www.nerdfonts.com/) set as the terminal font.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show_file("powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1", "powershell")
```

The R terminal in VS Code is radian, not PowerShell, so neither file affects it.

## git

The global git configuration (`~/.gitconfig`) only holds my name and e-mail address (`user.name`, `user.email`) and the [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/) filters that `git lfs install` adds:

```ini
[filter "lfs"]
    clean = git-lfs clean -- %f
    smudge = git-lfs smudge -- %f
    process = git-lfs filter-process
    required = true
[user]
    name = <your name>
    email = <your e-mail>
```

Everything else about git (autofetch, no sync confirmation, PR branches) is in the [VS Code settings](settings.qmd).

## PATH rules {#path-rules}

Most problems in this set-up came from `PATH`. The rules:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| `C:\Program Files\R\bin` (rig's shortcuts) is on `PATH`. | `R`, `Rscript` and radian then use rig's default version. |
| **No** version folder such as `C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.0\bin` on `PATH`. | It pins one R version and overrides rig. |
| **No** `R_HOME` environment variable (check both user and system). | Same: radian and R use it before anything else. |
| `Python312\` and `Python312\Scripts\` come **before** any other Python. | `python` and `radian` must be the 3.12 ones. Per-user folders (`C:\Users\...`) do not belong in the *system* `PATH`, where they win over the user `PATH`. |
| `C:\Program Files\Quarto\bin` comes before any per-user Quarto. | One Quarto, the current one. |
| After any change: quit and restart VS Code. | VS Code and its terminals keep the `PATH` they started with. |

To check what a **new** process will see, without restarting anything:

```powershell
$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "Machine") + ";" +
            [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
Get-Command R.exe, python, radian, quarto | Select-Object Name, Source
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("R_HOME", "User")
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("R_HOME", "Machine")
radian --version
```

## Package libraries

Each R version (major.minor) has its own user library, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\R\win-library\<x.y>`. R creates it on first use, so `rig system setup-user-lib` is not needed on Windows. R 4.5.0, 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 share `win-library\4.5`; R 4.6.x starts with an empty `win-library\4.6`. That is why the [R packages](install.qmd#the-r-packages) are installed once per R version.
